components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.model-density-invariance is not supplied for every assertion in the entry. The theorem asserts (body lines 136-137) that declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general. That is a claim that something fails in general, and no witness or argument for it appears in the annex proof (lines 97-104 prove only invariance under the transported prior and then restate scope) or anywhere in the body. Every other 'need not' claim in this chapter gets an explicit counterexample in its annex item. A secondary point: in the intrinsic weight identity, the claim that {sum_k alpha_k r_k > 0} has full Q_alpha-mass is asserted after 'similarly' (annex lines 84-85) with no written step.

defect_observations.observation: The theorem sentence 'Declaring a new flat prior in the new coordinates is not such a transport in general' (body 136-137) has no proof and no counterexample. The annex proves only the positive transport invariance. Supplying one bijection and prior whose pushforward is not flat would discharge it, for example the uniform prior on (0,1) under theta -> theta^2.

defect_observations.severity: minor, cited as a secondary gap
defect_observations.observation: 'The common factor similarly cancels in model weights where sum alpha_k r_k>0, a set of full Q_alpha-mass': the full-mass claim (dQ_alpha/dQ_* = sum alpha_k r_k, so its zero set is Q_alpha-null) is not written.

The annex item for thm:p15-nuisance-integration does not itself address the final sentence 'No equality of nuisance priors in different models is automatic'. It was accepted because each model's prior is a separate input under def:p15-model-comparison-experiment, the body (197-202) explains it, and the forward-referenced, proved kernel-version example (annex 360-375) is a witness.

The handbook's alpha_k are model prior probabilities summing to one. In the held source's eq. (16) (Sec. 6.1, p. 784, txt line 831), alpha_k = pr(H_k)/pr(H_0) is a prior odds against H_0. The chapter cites Sec. 6.1 without flagging the notational difference, and does not display the source's (K+1)-model form in terms of B_k0.
